title: Goal manipulation through policy-like language in invoice content
summary: Same sink and effect as FB-01. An invoice that should go to human review is approved for payment.

LC.rationale: Attacker-controlled invoice description free text is returned to the model inside a tool result and the model then calls approve_invoice, so language enters through ingested content and influences a privileged tool-invocation path.

CP.rationale: Each invoice starts a fresh message list, so there is no conversation memory; the invoice description is only re-retrieved source content and does not alter agent memory or standing behaviour.

AP.rationale: The effect is confined to the single FinBot agent and its own tool call; there are no handoffs, no other agents, and no trust-boundary crossing.

RH.rationale: The model can reach the approve_invoice write tool that sets status approved and payment_processed true, which is the reward/verifier channel on the path, but no human-verified reward-hacking episode is documented (prose walkthrough only, no payload or test).

ES.rationale: Five fixed tools are defined in code with no dynamic tools, MCP servers, plugins, or skills, and the binding is fixed and allowlisted outside model output.

agentic_applicability.rationale: The lab models FinBot as an autonomous invoice processing assistant that pursues natural-language goals and selects approve, reject, or escalate tool calls.
